old_problem: The literal label requests an SEL clear while the command invokes SDR clear. SDR definitions and SEL event history are distinct evidence stores: erasing either before the reads destroys a different part of the acceptance basis, and erasing SDR can impair sensor interpretation. The existing review also overstates the need for unknown raw bytes even though the source's validation path names standard high-level SDR, sensor and SEL read commands.
disposition_reason: Resolve the Engineering Decision Pending flag at the Review layer. ED-19 already forbids broad SEL destructive actions and requires immutable pre-action evidence plus exact targeted-delete semantics under separate approval. Authoritative ipmitool source confirms its SDR repository clear path performs SDRR erasure, while OpenBMC documentation distinguishes irreversible `sel clear` from record-specific `sel delete`. Therefore neither literal branch is permitted as setup for this read/correlation case. The original conflict and command remain historical source evidence, but the executable Review-layer scope is the complete non-destructive `sdr elist` + `sensor elist` + `sel elist` correlation. A future repository-clear objective, if genuinely required, must be a separately reviewed testcase with export/hash, erased-scope, postcondition and validated restore/rebuild recovery; it is not hidden inside this case.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1638, same-row DeepSeek/test-json fields, V2, historical V3.1 record, pending/conflict analyses, duplicate identity search and ED-01 through ED-30 rules were read. The actual next formal queue identity was reconstructed and directly opened as Functionality row 1663 / Wistron-BMC-00934-V003 / b7053c80de156ab7.

The upstream ipmitool SDR repository implementation sends the Clear SDR Repository storage operation and reports `SDRR successfully erased`; `sdr clear` is not an SEL-clear spelling variant. OpenBMC's ipmitool guidance separately documents `sel clear` as irreversible and `sel delete <number>` as single-event deletion.

ED-19 resolves the safety branch: preserve evidence first and never perform a broad clear as routine test setup. The criterion needs historical SEL evidence to determine whether abnormal sensor events occurred, so clearing it would make the claimed absence circular rather than prove health.

The source already supplies three standard read operations. No guessed raw payload is required to fulfill the named SDR/Sensor/SEL comparison; any private-script OEM extension must be documented and additive, never a prerequisite silently replacing these high-level reads.

Acceptance requires a project sensor truth matrix: stable sensor/record identity, physical component, units/scaling, thresholds, status, expected value/range or discrete state, freshness and allowed SEL events. These are runtime Project inputs under the user's parameterization rule, not a remaining Engineering Decision.

Complete outputs must be retained, not grep/head subsets. In-band and/or OOB target identity, protected credentials and time correlation are prerequisites; existing SEL/kernel/BMC evidence remains untouched.

ED-03/ED-13 permit standard BMC read drafts, ED-18 forbids invented thresholds, ED-19 controls destructive log actions, ED-26 forbids retry, and ED-33/ED-35/ED-36/ED-38 preserve Master/coverage and separate review completion from execution/verdict.

test_case.test_name: SDR Commands — preserved-repository sensor truth and SEL correlation
test_case.purpose: Read the complete SDR definitions, live sensor readings and SEL history from one verified BMC; map every in-scope record to real hardware and the approved sensor matrix; identify missing, stale, malformed, out-of-range or abnormal evidence without erasing SDR, SEL or other logs.
required_package: Supported `ipmitool` version and protected same-target IB/OOB transport with verified BMC/SUT/firmware identity; no inline secrets

Versioned platform sensor truth matrix covering required sensor/record IDs, physical component/entity, units/scaling, thresholds, expected range/discrete state, freshness, presence/optional rules and allowed abnormal events
Approved observation window and physical-state corroboration for relevant sensors, plus clock/timestamp mapping for SEL correlation
Complete SDR/SEL export and hash storage before reads, raw untruncated outputs, parser/schema provenance and restricted evidence location

If a future destructive clear is separately requested: a new owner decision, exact SEL record or SDR repository scope, pre-export/hash, postcondition, independent restore/rebuild recovery and separate review/authorization
test_case.test_command: Read-only only: capture and hash the complete current SDR and SEL repositories, then run the protected same-target equivalents of `ipmitool sdr elist`, `ipmitool sensor elist`, and `ipmitool sel elist`. Retain full raw output; correlate every in-scope SDR definition and live reading to the approved physical sensor matrix and analyze record-level SEL events for the defined observation window. Do not execute `ipmitool sdr clear`, `ipmitool sel clear`, broad log clearing, guessed raw commands or any destructive repository action in this testcase.
test_case.expected_result: Every required sensor/SDR record is present exactly as specified, maps to the correct physical component, uses the approved unit/scaling/threshold/status semantics, is fresh and reports the expected real state. SDR and Sensor views agree within the signed matrix, and SEL contains no unexplained disallowed sensor event during the approved window. Pre/post repository hashes and membership show that the read-only test caused no mutation.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS evidence requires complete record-level comparison against the signed matrix plus physical-state and SEL-window correlation; a successful command, empty SEL after deletion, generic `ok`, partial output or invented threshold is insufficient. Missing/extra/duplicate/stale/malformed records, unexplained unit/threshold/status/value differences, disallowed SEL events or repository mutation are reported for engineer FAIL/BLOCKED disposition. Project parameters may be bound at runtime, but absent authority cannot be replaced by guessed limits. The end user decides the DUT verdict.
safety_gate: Never run `sdr clear` under the source's Clear SEL label; never run `sel clear` or general log clearing to create a clean baseline.
Do not guess raw bytes, OEM decoding, thresholds, allowed events or sensor-to-hardware mappings; stop comparison when the signed matrix is incomplete.
Verify exact same-target BMC/SUT and protect credentials; do not expose secrets or accept truncated/cross-host/cached evidence.
Keep the run read-only: do not change sensor thresholds/event enables, BMC configuration, fan/power/device state or firmware.
Preserve the first inconsistent reading and all repositories; no automatic retry, repeated clear or BMC reset is permitted.
expected_evidence: Exact source identity and ED-19 disposition preserving the mislabeled `sdr clear` as prohibited historical source evidence
BMC/SUT/firmware/ipmitool/transport identity, approved sensor matrix, observation window and physical-state references
Immutable complete pre/post SDR and SEL exports/hashes plus untruncated `sdr elist`, `sensor elist` and `sel elist` outputs
Per-record identity/entity/component/unit/threshold/status/value/freshness comparison and record-level SEL event analysis
No-mutation/no-clear/no-retry audit and engineer-owned PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED verdict
test_case.recovery: The approved plan performs only reads. On missing sensors, repository hash/membership change, BMC instability or unexpected output, stop, preserve raw/export evidence and close the protected session; do not clear, reset or retry. If an unauthorized clear occurred, invoke only a previously validated vendor restore/rebuild procedure for that exact repository and escalate—never reconstruct SDR or SEL from assumptions.

source_conflict.reason: The Master mismatch remains preserved, but ED-19 and authoritative command semantics resolve the Review-layer execution choice: neither broad clear is permitted in this evidence-dependent read/correlation case; only the explicit high-level reads remain executable coverage.

blocked.reason: The safe operation, target class, evidence and recovery boundary are defined. Exact target and sensor matrix are bindable project prerequisites rather than unresolved core command semantics.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Verified BMC/SUT/firmware and protected transport; ipmitool version; signed sensor/SDR physical truth, unit/threshold/status/freshness matrix; observation window and allowed SEL events; full export/hash and evidence paths. Any future clear requires a separate new test/review contract.
pending.execution_status: REVIEW RESOLVED; EXECUTION NOT STARTED; NO SDR/SEL/LOG CLEAR, RAW WRITE, SENSOR/BMC/DUT OR OTHER HARDWARE ACTION AUTHORIZED OR EXECUTED

external_authorities.application: The SDR repository clear implementation issues repository erasure and reports SDRR erased, proving it is not an SEL-clear alias.
Documents `sel clear` as irreversible and distinguishes record-specific `sel delete <number>`, supporting ED-19 separation of broad clear from targeted deletion.
Provides the authoritative command family context for standard SDR, sensor and SEL operations; platform/OEM response semantics still require the Project matrix.

project_authority: The BMC/platform owner supplies target identity, sensor matrix and allowed-event policy; the lab/operator confirms relevant physical states; the evidence owner retains immutable exports; the end user decides verdict. A repository-clear owner may create a separate governed testcase but cannot reinsert broad clearing into this read/correlation case or modify Master history.
